Burns Night Supper

Your At-Home Burns Night Celebration

Gather your loved ones and prepare for a night of Scottish cheer! This agenda guides you through a warm and traditional Burns Night Supper, celebrating the life and works of Robert Burns from the comfort of your home.

  1. Afternoon

    Kitchen Preparations

    Start your culinary journey by preparing the hearty Cock-a-Leekie Soup, assembling the delightful Cranachan, and baking some crisp Oatcakes, getting a head start on your feast.

    Recipes: Cock-a-Leekie Soup · Cranachan · Traditional Scottish Oatcakes

  2. Late Afternoon

    Set the Scene

    Don your finest tartan (or simply something smart!), set your table with care, and put on some lively Scottish folk music to create a truly festive atmosphere.

  3. Early Evening

    A Warming Welcome

    As the evening draws in, pour a dram of smoky single malt whisky to warm the spirits and welcome the celebration ahead.

    Recipes: Smoky Single Malt Whisky for Burns Night

  4. Dinner Time

    Piping in the Haggis

    With a flourish, play some rousing bagpipe music (even from a speaker!) as you proudly bring the star of the show, the haggis, to the table.

  5. During Dinner

    Ode to the Haggis & Supper

    Before delving into the meal, deliver the 'Address to a Haggis' with passion, then enjoy the iconic haggis with neeps and tatties, alongside your comforting soup and oatcakes.

    Recipes: Haggis with Neeps and Tatties · Cock-a-Leekie Soup · Traditional Scottish Oatcakes

  6. After Main Course

    Toasts to the Bard and Beyond

    Raise your glass high for a toast to Robert Burns, and engage in the traditional 'Toast to the Lassies' (and perhaps a witty reply!) with another dram.

    Recipes: Smoky Single Malt Whisky for Burns Night

  7. Dessert

    A Sweet Scottish Ending

    Conclude your magnificent feast with the creamy, fruity delight of cranachan, a perfect sweet note to a rich meal.

    Recipes: Cranachan

  8. Evening's End

    Auld Lang Syne

    Gather everyone together to sing 'Auld Lang Syne,' a poignant and unifying end to a memorable evening celebrating Scottish heritage and friendship.

May your Burns Night be filled with warmth, good company, and the spirit of the Bard!
